findings.title: index.json open_findings count wrong — reports 15 but 8 findings are actually open
findings.detail: The top-level open_findings field in .audits/index.json reads 15. Counting findings by status in the array shows 8 open and 9 fixed after the 2026-07-09 audit run. The by_severity sub-object (IMPORTANT:13, COSMETIC:2) appears to reflect scan totals not open counts. Downstream tools that read open_findings for dashboards or the SessionStart banner will display an inflated count.
findings.fix_sketch: Set open_findings to 8, update by_severity to {CRITICAL:0,IMPORTANT:7,COSMETIC:1}, and set last_updated to today. Will be further corrected to 3 after today's fixes land.
findings.fix_summary: Updated open_findings to 3 (post-today fixes), by_severity to IMPORTANT:2/COSMETIC:1, last_updated to 2026-07-12T04:10:35Z, and fixed_this_run to 7.

findings.title: README.md Phase 3 elapsed/overdue counts 3 days stale — 49/35 days (2026-07-09) should be 52/38 (2026-07-12)
findings.detail: The Status table in README.md shows Phase 3 soak elapsed as 49 days and overdue count as 35 days, both computed as of 2026-07-09. Today is 2026-07-12, so elapsed is 52 days (from 2026-05-21 soak start) and the Phase 4 gate evaluation is 38 days overdue (from 2026-06-04 soak completion). Stale day counts erode trust in the status table.
findings.fix_sketch: Update '49 days elapsed' to '52 days elapsed' and '35 days overdue' to '38 days overdue' in the Phase 3 status row.
findings.fix_summary: Updated README.md Phase 3 row from '49 days elapsed / 35 days overdue' to '52 days elapsed / 38 days overdue' as of 2026-07-12.

findings.title: Phase 4 gate evaluation 38 days overdue — IFleet fold-in blocked
findings.detail: Phase 3 soak completed 2026-06-04. The go/no-go decision for Phase 4 (self-healing fingerprint + DRAFT auto-rules) was due then but remains unresolved as of 2026-07-12 — 38 days overdue. All five IFleet integration ADRs remain DRAFT. Any further nightly audit improvements in the elevation system risk being incompatible with the eventual IFleet fold-in shape if ADRs stay unreviewed.
findings.fix_sketch: Sebastian to review and make the Phase 4 go/no-go decision and answer the 5 ADR open questions. Agent can update day counts but cannot resolve the underlying decision.

findings.title: ADR-001 through ADR-005 each missing Date, Author, Decider in per-ADR metadata
findings.detail: docs/ifleet-integration-adrs.md has a top-level YAML frontmatter block but each individual ADR section (ADR-001 through ADR-005) only has a bold Status and Affects line. IFleet ADR convention (per docs/adr/ in IFleet) requires Date, Author, and Decider fields on each ADR. Without them, fold-in reviewers cannot determine ownership or when each decision was made.
findings.fix_sketch: Add Date, Author, and Decider bold metadata lines under each ADR heading, matching the values already in the file-level frontmatter (Date: 2026-05-20, Author: T1, Decider: Sebastian Puig pending).
findings.fix_summary: Added **Date**, **Author**, and **Decider** metadata lines to each of the five ADR sections in docs/ifleet-integration-adrs.md.

findings.title: ADR-Proposer-001 embedded in proposer-spec.md has no frontmatter at all
findings.detail: The ADR-Proposer-001 section in docs/proposer-spec.md starts with a heading and Status bold text only. No Date, Author, or Decider fields are present. This makes it the only ADR in the system with no metadata, inconsistent with both the IFleet ADR style and the ifleet-integration-adrs.md file-level frontmatter that covers ADR-001 through ADR-005.
findings.fix_sketch: Add Date, Author, and Decider bold metadata lines under the ADR-Proposer-001 heading, using values consistent with the file header (T5, 2026-05-20, Sebastian pending).
findings.fix_summary: Added **Date**, **Author**, and **Decider** metadata lines to the ADR-Proposer-001 section in docs/proposer-spec.md.

findings.title: Finding ID in 20260703T050000Z.json uses descriptive text not 8 hex chars
findings.detail: The finding ID in .audits/20260703T050000Z.json does not follow the AUDIT-<repo>-<8hexchars> schema specified in plan.md. Historical scan files are append-only and must not be mutated to preserve referential integrity. This is a data hygiene issue for future regression detection.
findings.fix_sketch: Do not mutate the historical file. Document the deviation in the finding and add a scanner validation check to prevent recurrence in future scans.

findings.title: ADR-004 suggests 30-min reap TTL but lane-scheduler-spec.md implements 60-min prune
findings.detail: ADR-004 open questions section suggests 'each entry has a heartbeat_ts field; scheduler reaps entries older than 30 minutes.' However lane-scheduler-spec.md's lane-prune-stale.sh already shipped with STALE_AFTER_SEC default 3600 (60 min). The ADR open question should be resolved to match the implementation.
findings.fix_sketch: Update ADR-004 open question to note that 60-min was implemented in lane-scheduler-spec.md and is the authoritative default. Mark the open question as resolved.
findings.fix_summary: Updated ADR-004 open question on Lane TTL to note that lane-scheduler-spec.md shipped with STALE_AFTER_SEC=3600 (60 min) as the default, superseding the 30-min suggestion.

findings.title: ADR-001 through ADR-005 use 3-digit numbering; IFleet ADR convention uses 4-digit
findings.detail: docs/ifleet-integration-adrs.md labels ADRs as ADR-001 through ADR-005 using 3-digit numbers. IFleet's docs/adr/ directory uses 4-digit numbering (0001, 0002, etc.). The inconsistency is low-risk but would require renaming all cross-references at fold-in time. Deferred to Phase 6 fold-in per prior audit.
findings.fix_sketch: At Phase 6 fold-in time, rename ADR-001 through ADR-005 to 0001 through 0005 and update all cross-references in the file. Do not rename now — it would create unnecessary churn before the fold-in plan is approved.
